newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh to get $105 million World Bank credit.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh to get $105 million World Bank credit.

text.p: The World Bank, one of Bangladesh's major donors, on Wednesday approved a $105 million concessional loan to finance a poverty alleviation project, a bank statement said.

It said the money would be provided to Palli Karma Sahayak Foundation (PKSF) for offering loans to an estimated 1.2 million poor and mostly female borrowers through more than 100 non-governmental orgainisations (NGOs).
The loan, carrying a nominal interest, is payable in 40 years. Under terms of the credit, the government will lend the fund to PKSF at 1.0-percent interest for 20 years, with five years garce priod.

The PKFS will then relend to the NGOs at 3-4 percent interest. "The partner organisations (NGOs) will be free to set the final lending rates to the beneficiaries (expected to be in 25-30 percent ragnge)," the statement said.
The PKSF, a quasi-government agency, has more than 120 partner organisations dedicated to microcredit programmes.
The World Bank credit will finance 77 percent of the $136 million poverty alleviation project.

A recent World Bank report said Bangladeshi women were subject to employment discrimination. "Even in South Asia, Bangladesh has one of the lowest female economic activity rates (11 percent)," it said.
Nearly half of Bangladesh's 120 million people live below poverty. The country's annual per capita income is about $260, according to official figures.
